headline: Light rain Saturday night into Sunday, then a cool, mostly dry stretch next week.
summary: A weak low-pressure system is approaching from British Columbia, bringing a short spell of light rain to western Washington. Rain arrives on the coast Saturday afternoon and spreads inland Saturday night into Sunday morning, mostly affecting the Olympic Peninsula and areas west of the Cascades. Totals will vary: the coast and the west-facing Olympic slopes could see the most, while Puget Sound gets very little. Showers end Sunday morning, leaving cloudy skies and highs in the 50s. Next week stays cool and cloudy, with the system staying offshore through midweek. A weak disturbance brings a slight chance of light rain Tuesday, and drier weather follows Wednesday through Friday. Forecasters are watching a possibly more active pattern around October 31 to November 6, but that is far off and uncertain.
